text.p: Philippine Asia Equity Inc on Tuesday reiterated its sell recommendation on oil refiner Petron Corp saying the firm's margins would be squeezed.

"We have increased our net income forecast by 12 percent for 1997 and 1998 ... and sales demand growth figures were adjusted upward from 5.4 percent to 6.4 percent per annum. Despite the improvement in the bottom line, Petron remains a sell," analyst Regina Manzano said.
She said the return on equity ratio has declined to 25 percent last year from 32 percent in 1993, and would continue to decline in the future.
The recent deregulation of the oil industry, which has attracted 31 new players from the previous three, would further squeeze its margin, Manzano said.
Huge capital expenditure to keep its lead in the market could dent its cashflow in the coming years. On the other hand, price increase would be difficult to implement.
"Petroleum products will remain politically sensitive, and as such, price increases will always be subject to intense public scrutiny," Manzano said.
